observation: Source object/surface/line structure and source tags are machine-readable; seal surfaces must remain separate from their parent accounts.
The acquired Akkadian cohort includes letters, administrative accounts, damaged passages and Sumerian formulae. Whole edited records and readable lines have different coverage.
The inspected Qubbet el Hawa vessel No. 89/136 (259) has a five-token source text including a commodity and named people linked by kinship terminology. Its source dating bounds are -2363 and -2187.
Edition extent and source token IDs do not always agree across the two transformed Egyptian corpora. The complete-vessel cohort requires agreement.
Displayed uncertainty/restoration can be absent from normalized search-link strings. Final eligibility checks both representations.
Fischer presents Old Kingdom seals combining royal names and official titles with decorative figures. These supply a qualitative name/title comparison, outside the measured jar cohort.
Rao et al. already compared IVS with Sumerian, Old Tamil and Vedic Sanskrit. Their supplementary Sumerian dataset is drawn from literary compositions.
The existing full-register clean-text benchmark supplies 1,593 distinct IVS faces of length 3-12, with 7,970 codes and no supplied meanings.
